authorityClasses.name: workspace-only
authorityClasses.description: May change ephemeral workspace files but cannot mutate remote repositories, clusters, cloud resources, or other external systems.

authorityClasses.name: read-only
authorityClasses.description: Adds explicitly selected non-production inspection and planning access while retaining the external-mutation prohibition.

trustBoundaries.name: browser-client
trustBoundaries.role: Authenticated but untrusted source of workspace commands and recipient of workspace output.
trustBoundaries.boundary: May hold a revocable client session but never receives workload, repository, or platform identities.

trustBoundaries.name: client-access-adapter
trustBoundaries.role: Terminates client transport and authenticates browser access before forwarding to T3.
trustBoundaries.boundary: Must not convert client identity into infrastructure authority inside the workspace.

trustBoundaries.name: workspace-runtime
trustBoundaries.role: One T3 server and its provider subprocesses operating on selected workspace state.
trustBoundaries.boundary: T3 and provider CLIs share the workspace authority ceiling and are isolated from other workspaces and the host.

trustBoundaries.name: repository-content
trustBoundaries.role: Selected source material and instructions treated as untrusted input to tools and agents.
trustBoundaries.boundary: Repository content cannot select mounts, credentials, egress, RBAC, or a stronger profile.

trustBoundaries.name: kubernetes-control-plane
trustBoundaries.role: Enforces workload identity, RBAC, pod security, storage, resources, and network policy.
trustBoundaries.boundary: Workspace service accounts cannot alter their own enforcement resources or authority ceiling.

trustBoundaries.name: external-services
trustBoundaries.role: Provider, Git, package, Kubernetes, and cloud APIs outside the workspace boundary.
trustBoundaries.boundary: Access requires an explicit egress purpose and separately scoped identity where authentication is needed.

requiredAdapters.name: kubernetes-workspace
requirements: standard workload, Service, ConfigMap, Secret reference, PVC, RBAC, and NetworkPolicy APIs
exactly one T3 server for each writable T3 state boundary
restricted pod security, non-root execution, dropped capabilities, and bounded resources

requiredAdapters.name: client-access
requirements: authenticated and encrypted browser access
revocable client sessions and pairing material
no direct exposure of the unauthenticated T3 service

requiredAdapters.name: repository-source
requirements: explicit repository and revision selection
read-only remote credentials for v0
no ambient host checkout mount

requiredAdapters.name: provider-authentication
requirements: provider state attached at runtime rather than built into images
revocable authentication scoped independently from infrastructure identity
no credential values in profile metadata or agent instructions

requiredAdapters.name: workspace-storage
requirements: isolated writable state for one workspace
single-writer attachment for T3 state
declared retention, expiry, deletion, and backup behavior

requiredAdapters.name: identity-and-egress
requirements: default-deny egress resolved from declared purposes
short-lived workload identity where platform access is enabled
read-only non-production authority for platform-readonly

requiredAdapters.name: lifecycle-and-audit
requirements: create, inspect, connect, revoke, expire, and destroy operations
audit records contain metadata and outcomes but no credential values or repository content
destruction revokes access before deleting retained state according to policy

invariants.statement: Exactly one T3 server may write a T3 state boundary.
Only declared repositories and revisions enter a workspace.
Images and long-lived workspace configuration contain no decryption identities or broad static credentials.
Network access is denied unless an adapter resolves a declared purpose to an approved destination.
Workspace processes run non-root without privilege, host namespaces, host paths, or container sockets.
Repository content, browser input, provider output, and workspace processes cannot increase the selected profile authority ceiling.

nonGoals: remote repository push or pull-request publication from v0 workspaces
high availability for a single workspace T3 server
multiple mutually distrusting users inside one workspace
ambient access to host files, host credentials, or organization-wide checkouts
secret decryption or general-purpose credential brokerage inside the agent runtime
guaranteeing confidentiality of data intentionally sent to an approved AI provider
